item.title: 'Am I supposed to answer that?' - Erling Haaland SNAPS at interviewers over Manchester City’s 114 Premier League charges
item.description: FBL-EUR-NATIONS-NOR-WAL - AFP Erling Haaland delivered a blunt response to questions regarding the ongoing legal battle surrounding Manchester City’s 114 Premier League charges. Although the Norwegian striker was in no mood to discuss the club's financial investigation following his goalscoring exploits on international duty, he still went on to offer a lengthy reply. Haaland pushes back during post-match TV interview Norway claimed a 3-1 home victory over Wales in the Nations League, with Manchester City forward Haaland contributing both a goal and an assist. Immediately after the final whistle, the striker faced live television questions from Norwegian broadcaster TV2 regarding the off-pitch turmoil at the Etihad Stadium. City are currently appealing an independent commission's verdict that found them guilty of 114 serious breaches of Premier League financial rules between 2009 and 2018. Despite the club maintaining their innocence throughout the dispute, Haaland made clear that he felt unqualified to address a legal matter spanning his childhood years. Striker lists youth career before questioning line of inquiry Responding directly to the TV2 reporter, Haaland walked through his early playing days in Norway to highlight his lack of involvement during the investigated nine-season window. "The investigation covered 2009 to 2018. In 2009, I played for Bryne U-9s. In 2010, the U-10s; in 2011, the U-11s; in 2012, the U-12s; in 20-13, the U13s. Shall we continue? We don't need the whole list," he said. He continued: "2014, the U-14s; 2015, the U-15s and the national team, then the U-16s, I think. In 2016, I moved up to Bryne's first team, second team and youth team. In 2017, I went to Molde. In 2018, I was with Molde: the first team, Molde 2 and a bit with the youth team." Haaland then questioned why he was being pressed on the dispute, noting: "So this is a question I struggle to answer because it's a legal battle... It's a case between the Premier League and Manchester City that a panel will deal with. Am I supposed to answer that? I'm not really sure. But it's a difficult question to answer when I don't really know that much about it. I assume the answers will come... I don't know when. I haven't read much about it." Long-term City commitment remains intact While Haaland recalled former Norwegian City players from that era - naming Abdisalam Ibrahim, Martin Samuelsen, Omar Elabdellaoui, and Kjetil Haug - he insisted the proceedings do not affect his future in Manchester. "To be completely honest, I'm focused on trying to perform for Manchester City. A club I signed a five-year deal with in 2022 and a new nine-and-a-half-year deal in late 2024. I think that says everything about the matter. I'm a City player, and I'm incredibly happy there," he stated. item.title: Former Manchester United and Everton midfielder Morgan Schneiderlin claims 'incredible' Arsenal star William Saliba 'simply cannot turn down' Real Madrid
item.description: SK Slavia Praha v Arsenal FC - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 - Getty Images Sport Former Manchester United and Everton midfielder Morgan Schneiderlin believes Arsenal defender William Saliba will find it impossible to reject Real Madrid. Having played alongside his compatriot at Nice in 2021, the retired Frenchman expects the centre-back to be tempted once an approach arrives. French defender attracts Spanish giants Schneiderlin has worried Arsenal supporters by warning that Saliba will struggle to resist the Bernabeu when an inevitable transfer pursuit ignites. Signed from Saint-Etienne for £27 million in 2019 , the France international has developed into one of Europe's best centre-backs under Mikel Arteta. Persistent links to the Spanish giants even prompted Arteta to discuss the speculation with the player last season. Former team-mate praises elite mentality Although the defender revealed during those talks with his manager that he was happy with life at the Emirates Stadium, his former Ligue 1 colleague believes a switch to Spain could prove too alluring. Now 37 and having retired in 2024, Schneiderlin witnessed his compatriot's rise first-hand during their single season together on the French Riviera and is convinced he has become a world-class talent. Speaking to ComeOn , the ex-midfielder said: "William Saliba to Real Madrid? That's something he will need to decide for himself. It's not for me to say whether he should stay at Arsenal or go to Madrid but what I do know, having played alongside him, is that he is a top centre-back with an elite mentality who always wants to improve. He's coming back from a long injury now, but I think the bigger question is actually for Arsenal: if you lose Saliba, who do you replace him with?" Replacement headache looms for Gunners Convinced the Gunners would face a major dilemma trying to replace such an influential figure at the heart of their defence, Schneiderlin recalled advising elite clubs to sign the youngster long before his valuation soared. Expanding on the pull of Los Blancos, he continued: "There are very few centre-backs in the world right now capable of delivering those kinds of performances. I said this many years ago when he was playing for Nice, if I were a big club, I would buy him immediately, because down the line his price tag would become far too high. "He is an incredible player to have in your side. But when a decision like that comes up, there are a handful of clubs in your career that you simply cannot turn down, and Real Madrid is one of them." Fitness boost precedes Tyneside trip Saliba has now returned to action following a spell on the sidelines with a back issue. However, the defender was omitted from the France squad for this month's Nations League clashes against Italy and Turkey. He is nevertheless expected to be fully fit when Arsenal visit Newcastle United in the Premier League on November 21.

item.title: 'It's absolutely huge!' – Erling Haaland fires Norway past Wales as Craig Bellamy's men suffer Nations League heartbreak
item.description: FBL-EUR-NATIONS-NOR-WAL - AFP Erling Haaland contributed a goal and an assist as Norway defeated Wales 3-1 in Oslo to leapfrog Craig Bellamy's side in Group A4. The result leaves Wales facing a relegation play-off in March, while Haaland celebrated a massive milestone for his national team. Haaland inspires Norway to victory over Wales in Oslo Erling Haaland played a decisive role as Norway secured a vital 3-1 victory over Wales in Oslo, avenging last month's defeat in Cardiff and condemning Craig Bellamy's side to the bottom of UEFA Nations League Group A4. After a goalless first half where Wales created the better chances, the hosts turned the screw after the break. Antonio Nusa broke the deadlock on the hour mark before combining with Haaland to set up substitute Andreas Schjelderup for Norway's second. Although David Brooks pulled a goal back with a delicate chipped finish, Haaland sealed the result from the penalty spot. Haaland hails 'absolutely huge' win after milestone strike The victory marked a significant turning point for Norway's golden generation after a challenging campaign that saw them drop to the foot of the group prior to kick-off. For Haaland, netting his 66th international goal from just 60 caps further cemented his legendary status. Reflecting on the hard-fought triumph and the journey of the national team, Haaland expressed his immense pride to TV2 Norway : "It's absolutely huge. We've been on a fantastic journey together... It's something really special to be part of." Nusa and Bellamy reflect on high-intensity battle Match-winner Antonio Nusa admitted that Norway had to weather a difficult storm in the first half before finding their rhythm after the interval. "It was a tough start for us, I'm not going to lie. I felt we couldn't really find our rhythm. Scoring the first goal helped, then came the second and the third. It was absolutely fantastic," Nusa said. Meanwhile, Wales boss Craig Bellamy took pride in his side's brave approach in Oslo , despite costly lapses in concentration. "We wanted to take the game to Norway here. We didn't want to just sit back. I always thought we were in the game and there were really good moments from us," Bellamy told BBC Sport. "It was just our final ball, at times, could have been better... In that period just after half-time, we dropped our intensity a bit." Relegation play-offs loom for Wales The defeat means Wales will finish bottom of Group A4 regardless of their final fixture at home against reigning champions Portugal on Tuesday. With an inferior head-to-head record against Norway and Denmark, Bellamy's men are almost certain to face a League B relegation play-off in March. Furthermore, the outcome confirms that Wales will miss out on being among the top seeds for the Euro 2028 qualifying draw. As Norway celebrate preserving their top-tier status behind Haaland's brilliance, Wales must regroup ahead of a challenging spring.

item.title: Mo-hits! Last-ball boundary seals U19 Asia Cup triumph for India
item.description: Mohit Ulva! Remember the name! When India needed a miracle, when the Pakistan team could almost touch the trophy and when the Under-19 Asia Cup final seemed to be slipping away, the young allrounder produced an innings that will be remembered for a long, long time. India were staring at defeat at 252/8 in the 42nd over, chasing a daunting 338 against Pakistan at the Al Amerat Cricket Ground on Saturday. But Ulva had other ideas. What followed was an extraordinary display of nerve, power and belief as India pulled off a sensational last-ball, one-wicket victory to lift the title. At the heart of India’s remarkable escape was the unlikely alliance between No. 7 Manal Chauhan and No. 10 Ulva. With 87 runs required from the last 51 deliveries, the pair refused to surrender. They took the attack to the Pakistan bowlers, who had been disciplined for much of the innings but began to lose their bearings under pressure. Chauhan was magnificent in his counter-attacking 47 off 32. He brought an urgency to India’s chase, giving Ulva the perfect partner in a partnership worth 57 off just 5.5 overs. Their stand transformed the contest, dragging India back from the brink. But an India-Pakistan game cannot be without its fair share of twists and turns. Pakistan struck with Chauhan’s wicket in the 48th over, leaving India needing 29 off 16. Enter Chiragupati Venakata. Playing his first match of the tournament, the No. 11 showed remarkable composure to stand his ground alongside Ulva. There was no panic, no attempt to play beyond his limitations. He simply gave his partner the support he needed while Ulva continued to believe that the impossible was possible. 135849181 The final two overs brought the kind of drama that makes India-Pakistan encounters special. India needed 25 off 12 and Ulva managed to keep the chase alive, smashing Mohammad Sayyam for 17 runs. With eight required off the final over, Ulva held his nerve and found the boundary when it mattered the most, finishing the job with a lofted shot off the final delivery. It was the highest successful chase in Youth ODI history. Ulva was deservedly named Player of the Match. Brief scores: India 339/9 (Rachandani 80, Sehwag 58; Rizwanullah 3-53) beat Pakistan 337/9 (Usman 107, Qadir 80; Kavya 4-68) by 1 wicket.

item.title: “Worst Starting QB in College Football”: Fans Want Sam Leavitt Benched As Lane Kiffin Falls to His Knees After LSU QB’s Third INT vs. Texas
item.description: LSU Tigers quarterback Sam Leavitt. © Imagn via Reuters Connect LSU head coach Lane Kiffin literally dropped to his knees in disappointment with quarterback Sam Leavitt’s performance against the Texas Longhorns on Saturday in Baton Rouge. ESPN shared Kiffin’s disappointed look after Leavitt threw an end-zone interception in the third quarter with just over 12 minutes remaining. Texas DB Jelani McDonald returned the end-zone pick for a touchback. Leavitt’s third interception ended the entire LSU drive as the Tigers failed to extend their four-point lead. Fans reacted to Kiffin’s reaction to Leavitt’s interception on X. “Sam Leavitt is the worst starting QB in college football,” one fan wrote. “You know how bad you gotta be to have Lane Kiffin praying to God while on his knees😭,” one fan joked. “Sam Leavitt genuinely might be the worst quarterback in the SEC; I don’t even care. And I am fully aware that Marcel Reed exists,” one fan commented. “You gotta bench Sam Leavitt, I’m sorry,” one fan wrote. “Bench Sam Leavitt. He is losing you the game. He has lost you previous games,” one fan remarked. “Bench him,” one fan added. Sam Leavitt Has 3 INTs In 3 Quarters Against Texas In the blockbuster SEC clash against Texas, LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt struggled to throw passes accurately. In the first quarter, with under two minutes remaining, Leavitt’s pass was tipped and intercepted by Jelani McDonald, giving Texas possession at its own 32-yard line. McDonald picked off another Leavitt pass in the end zone at the start of the second quarter. Under pressure, the LSU quarterback threw into an area with no receiver, ending a promising drive. The third interception came in the third quarter with just over a dozen minutes remaining. For the third time in a row across the quarters, Leavitt’s throw was intercepted by the same man, McDonald. The end-zone interception ended LSU’s five-play, 59-yard drive. At the time, LSU led 14-10, and they could have extended the lead from four points to 11. LSU redeemed itself before the quarter ended as Dilin Jones rushed the ball from the left for a 44-yard touchdown. Despite Leavitt’s struggles, Texas has trailed for most of the game. The Tigers’ quarterback has also thrown two touchdowns while completing 27 of 37 passes for 244 yards. Meanwhile, Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning threw three interceptions and zero touchdowns while completing 18 of 32 passes for 170 yards. item.title: ‘I’ve got a ton of respect for those guys’: What Arizona coach Brent Brennan said after losing a shootout to No. 2 Utah
item.description: Arizona running back Kedrick Reescano (3) scores a touchdown against Utah in the first half of an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026, in Tucson, Ariz. | Rick Scuteri, Associated Press It was a back-and-forth game that saw seven lead changes late Saturday night in Tucson, where Brent Brennan’s Arizona Wildcats ultimately fell short against the No. 2 Utah Utes, 40-39. Brennan’s quarterback, Noah Fifita, threw for 356 yards and three touchdowns, but it was not enough against Devon Dampier’s 204-yard, two-touchdown passing night that included 100 yards on the ground and two rushing touchdowns. Arizona’s defense also had no answers it seemed against Daniel Bray, who recorded his highest career rushing game with 197 yards and a touchdown. Casino Del Sol atmosphere Brennan began his postgame press conference by acknowledging the crowd’s energy. “I want to say thank you to our fans, our alums, our students. I mean, that’s something that we challenged everybody with all week, and they showed up tonight. They were on their feet all night. It led to four false start penalties for Utah,” he said. “It was just an awesome atmosphere in there. That’s something we’ve talked about a lot, about how do we create the best atmosphere in the Big 12, and I thought our fans did that tonight.” When asked how the later start because of Friday’s FAA grounding affected his team he said, “Nothing really changed for us. We had the benefit of having a home game, and they moved the game three hours.” Brennan mentioned that he was worried the three-hour delay would hurt the crowd’s attendance and excitement, but those worries were quickly put to rest for the coach now in his third year at Arizona. “That was one of the best parts about it. You move the game three hours, our students were there all night on their feet, they never sat down. item.title: “They’re Gonna Get Destroyed by the Lions”: NFL Fans React to Mike Vrabel Drinking Beer With Patriots Fans in Munich Before Sunday Game
item.description: Source: Imagn Mike Vrabel couldn’t hide his excitement about returning to Germany, but some were concerned by his antics. On Saturday, a day before his New England Patriots were to face the Detroit Lions in Munich, the former linebacker-turned-head coach was spotted drinking a mug of beer with some fans at a pub: Reaction to his spree, however, was decidedly negative: The drinking binge capped off a week of enjoyment for Vrabel, who also spoke to a few young flag football players during an NFL-run clinic. For his closing remarks , he said (via Boston.com): “I knew we had fans in Germany, but I didn’t know we had this many fans. Thank you for your support, go Pats, let’s raise a glass to everybody.” Interestingly, Lions chief owner and chairwoman Sheila Ford Hamp was also at the pub. When approached by the media, she said (via Nolan Bianchi’s X): “I was actually looking for Patriots fans today, just out of curiosity. I think I saw two.” Mike Vrabel gets candid on roster before Lions clash in Munich Sunday will mark the Patriots’ second straight game against an NFC North team and third in four, as well as their last game before their bye week. And Mike Vrabel had some stern words for the roster on Friday (via ESPN): “We’re always looking for guys that are looking for ways in as opposed to ways out. At this point in the season, 10 weeks straight without a bye, there’s pretty much nobody out there that’s 100 percent. We have to realize that, we have to recognize that, we also have to find ways to do our job.” Kickoff for the game against the Lions is at 9:30 a.m. ET on Fox. item.title: Reality dawns after Wales dared to dream
item.description: Did that really happen? Or was it just a dream? As Welsh rugby fans wake up on Sunday morning the realisation will dawn on them. It has happened. Wales have finally beaten the All Blacks again. For the first time in 73 years - after 34 defeats - 19 December 1953 is now joined by 14 November 2026 as a defining date in Welsh rugby history. Thousands of young kids will this morning be turning up to rugby training or matches, driven by parents who have a hint of a headache, with this magical day fresh in the memory. Steve Tandy‘s heroes will always have this moment, with inspirational captain Dewi Lake and player-of-the-match James Botham shedding tears. "Best day of my life," concluded Wales centre Eddie James. Many will concur. Wales were awarded the Raeburn Shield - presented to rugby's lineal champions - after the 35-28 win against New Zealand [Getty Images] Why nobody was expecting a Wales win It was a result that sent shockwaves throughout Wales but also around the sporting world. Friends and relatives who had not been in contact for ages messaged each other to revel in or discuss the result. People reminisced that their parents or grandparents never saw this day. There was jubilation in Cardiff but also disbelief at the timing and magnitude of the occasion. Welsh rugby has been in disarray since the end of the 2023 World Cup after so many of the golden generation retired. The Wales men’s national team slumped to a record 18 straight Test defeats in a winless run that lasted 16 months as the side slipped to a lowest world ranking of 14th. Tandy had only won four Tests in 13 matches, those victories coming against Japan twice, Fiji and Italy. His side had been hammered twice by world champions South Africa without scoring a point and conceding 116. So when they awoke on Saturday morning hardly anybody outside the camp would have thought this Welsh team would succeed where previous Grand Slam-winning sides had failed to topple New Zealand. There had been hope, even occasional expectation, before previous contests. That was generally not the feeling this time around, as Wales - ranked 10th in the world - took on a New Zealand side that were ranked top before kick-off in Cardiff. So where does this staggering result stand in Welsh rugby history? There have been some wonderful days, with Grand Slam successes clinched in Cardiff in 1976, 1978, 2005, 2008, 2012 and 2019. Then there was the 30-3 drubbing of England in Cardiff in 2013 to clinch the Six Nations title, while Warren Gatland's side defeated the same opponents two years later at Twickenham in the World Cup.
